correctness.rationale: The code definition is a rank-five field-power parity check. Exhaustive primitive-polynomial checking proves all six primitive cyclic realizations are represented. A complete 31-coordinate syndrome-and-boundary transfer enumerates all 2^26 kernel words per code without omission or repetition, and an algebraically different signed-character transfer produces the same 18 full arrays. Both standalone package scripts check coefficient equality, dimensions, moments, reciprocal symmetry and three distinct classes; all exact bounded loops terminate. Direct exhaustive lower-dimension tests also agree. No infinite extrapolation is claimed.

evidence: Shi–Özbudak–Solé (2021), full-text Sections IV–V: specialized exact enumerators assume a single nonzero cyclotomic coset; code dimension is then at most five at length 31, unlike dimension twenty-six here.
Its general stability theorem applies to b at least the code dimension, and hence not to b=2,3,4.
Vega (2023) treats irreducible cyclic codes by irreducible parity-check polynomials, not Hamming codes whose irreducible polynomial is the generator.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A general theory providing bounds, a finite DP procedure in principle, or exact enumerators for different code classes does not logically imply these exact output coefficients without a specialization that has not been supplied. The displayed hypotheses explicitly exclude the current code dimension and read length.

The closest full-text arbitrary cyclic-code result has exact-enumerator hypotheses inapplicable to these dimension-26 Hamming codes at b<=4. value.rationale: Among binary primitive cyclic Hamming realizations, degree five is the first field degree with three distinct reciprocal primitive-polynomial pairs; the natural full family is classified, not an arbitrary subfamily. These codes have identical ordinary Hamming spectra yet three different complete overlapping-read spectra, providing exact multiplicity data needed for distinguishing cyclic implementations where minimum distance alone loses information.
